title: Genome‐wide association studies identified variants for taurine concentration in Japanese Black beef

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We performed genome‐wide association studies (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">GWAS</jats:styled-content>) using the Bovine<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>50 array to detect significant single nucleotide polymorphisms (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s) that may affect the concentration of 22 free amino acids and three peptides in Japanese Black beef cattle. A total of 574 Japanese Black cattle and 40,657 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s from the array were used for this study. Genome‐wide significant <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s were detected for β‐alanine (three <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s on chromosomes 22 and 29) and taurine (26 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s on chromosome 22). Importantly, the top two <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s for taurine were highly significant (<jats:italic>p </jats:italic>=<jats:italic> </jats:italic>6.2 × 10<jats:sup>−21</jats:sup>), and the frequency of the increase‐concentration allele (<jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>) for taurine was found to be 0.73. The <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic> allele frequency of this population was similar to that of the other unrelated Japanese Black cattle, but different from that of the other breeds. In addition, the significant <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s were not associated with carcass traits or fatty acid compositions. Interestingly, the top three of the four most significant <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s for taurine were located near solute carrier family 6, member 6 <jats:italic>(SLC6A6)</jats:italic>, which is a membrane transporter for taurine. We also found two associated variants in the 5′‐upstream region of <jats:italic>SLC6A6</jats:italic>; however, they were less significantly associated than the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>s from the Bovine<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP</jats:styled-content>50 array.</jats:p>
